title: Two pools, both reached
prompt: It is 10:20 ET. Read the chart and decide.

intro.beginner: Two pools of liquidity sit below price. Consider what each target would risk and reward, and whether one is the only right answer.

whyNot.label: only calling one target right
whyNot.why: Both pools are reached here. The equal lows give a clean 2R, and the previous day low follows for much more. A target at either is defensible; the process question is whether you chose one deliberately.

reference.summary: A valid short with two acceptable targets, both reached: the equal lows printed on the way down (internal, a clean 2R) and the previous day low (external, a much larger move). Either is a defensible draw.

bias.why: Lower highs and lower lows on the Daily and 4H; the overnight rally was a retrace.

decision.why: Sweep, displacement and a retrace into the gap: a valid short.

take.why: Valid, with a choice of targets.

draw.why: Equal lows just below are the nearest pool; the previous day low is the farther one.

annotations.label: Equal lows 21,260.5
annotations.why: Internal liquidity: two lows at the same price, close and obvious. A clean first target.
annotations.decisionNote: A 2R at a pool price has just printed.

annotations.label: Previous day low 21,236.25
annotations.why: External liquidity: the larger pool, reached after the internal one.
annotations.decisionNote: The runner if you hold past the first pool.

annotations.label: Overnight high 21,424.5
annotations.why: Buy-side liquidity swept at the open.

trade.confirmationLabel: the displacement that closed below the last 5m low

lookFor: More than one target can be right. Say which pool you're after and why, then stay with it.
A near target gives certainty and a far one gives size. Both are decisions about what the move is for.
